objects.original: Initialized drift rows plus completed coordinate Itô integrals, a compact-range Euclidean process X, a C¹ test, progressive L² derivative-weighted integrands θ and their finite-sum martingale M.
objects.reconstructed: State coordinate type I and Brownian coordinate type J; x,b,eta; process X; compact K with supplied fallback∈K; scalar f; existential integrands theta indexed by I×J and their summed integral M.

domains.original: Finite state and Brownian coordinate sets with decidable equality; finite sample measure, usual filtration and positive horizon; initial coordinates are F₀-measurable and drift coordinates are scalar progressive processes.
domains.reconstructed: Omega is measurable with finite measure mu and a filtration F indexed by nonnegative reals. T>0 is fixed. The Euclidean coordinate type J is finite with decidable equality. B:[0,infinity)×Omega→R^J. lambda_T denotes the pullback under NNReal.toReal of Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T]. I is finite with decidable equality. x:Omega→(I→R); b_i scalar processes; eta_ij progressive L² integrands; f:R^I→R; K⊆R^I.

assumptions.original: The horizon T is positive and the sample measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and the standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure. The state and Brownian coordinate types are finite with decidable equality. Each diffusion entry is progressive and square-integrable in the product of sample and horizon time measures. The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T]. Each initial coordinate is strongly measurable at time zero. Each drift coordinate is strongly progressive and has almost surely integrable time sections on the horizon. The scalar test is continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.
assumptions.reconstructed: Assumptions: B starts at zero for every omega, has jointly independent increments over disjoint half-open intervals, every continuous real linear functional ell sends B_t-B_s (s<t) to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||², and paths are continuous mu-a.e. B is strongly adapted to F and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. A progressive L² integrand is a real process a(t,omega), strongly progressive for F, for which (omega,t)↦a(t,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). Each x_i is strongly measurable for F_0. Every b_i is strongly progressive and is lambda_T-integrable pathwise mu-a.e. K is compact, fallback∈K, and f is ambient C¹ at every x∈K. The range assumption is mu-a.e. omega, for every t≤T, X(t,omega)∈K.

conclusion.original: Take the almost surely compact-range Euclidean process built from initialized drift time primitives and completed stochastic integrals. For a continuously Fréchet differentiable test on that range, the left-endpoint derivative sums converge in measure to the integral of the derivative applied to the drift vector plus the terminal value of a genuine martingale. Formula: \sum_k Df(X_{t_k})[\Delta_kX]\xrightarrow{\mu}\int_{[0,T]}Df(X_s)[b(s)]\,ds+M_T.
conclusion.reconstructed: Conclusion: I_j(a)(t,omega) denotes the specified completed Ito integral driven by the scalar coordinate B^j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j. Its representative is the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic integrals off the null complement of their uniform Cauchy event, and zero on that complement; it is held constant after T. Set X_i(t)=x_i+∫b_i(s)d lambda_t(s)+∑_j I_j(eta_ij)(t). There exists theta:I×J→progressive L² integrands such that, on one mu-full set, for every (i,j) and every t≥0, theta_{i,j}(t,omega)=Df(X(min(t,T),omega))[e_i] eta_ij(t,omega). Define M(t)=∑_{(i,j)∈I×J}I_j(theta_{i,j})(t). Then M is an F-martingale, M(0,omega)=0 for every omega, and ∑_{r=0}^{2^n-1}Df(X(t_r^n))[X(t_{r+1}^n)-X(t_r^n)] converges in mu-measure to ∫Df(X(s))[(b_i(s))_i]d lambda_T(s)+M(T), where t_r^n=rT/2^n.

quantifiers.original: For all setup data satisfying confinement, there exists θ with a.e. all-index/all-time process identity; its defined finite sum M is a martingale, vanishes at zero pointwise and supplies the terminal stochastic contribution.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Quantifier order: For every setup and f C¹ at each point of K, if X(t,omega) lies in K for all t≤T on one full-measure set, there exists a family theta_{i,j} of progressive L² integrands with the all-time process equality, and its defined sum M satisfies the remaining claims.

scopes.original: Convergence in measure at fixed T; θ equality holds on one full-measure set simultaneously for all indices and all t≥0 with the derivative evaluated at X(min(t,T)); M is a genuine global-time martingale and M₀=0 for every sample.
scopes.reconstructed: Scope: Theta's equality is a.e. omega simultaneously for every index and all nonnegative t, with X stopped at T in the derivative factor. The convergence is in measure at the fixed horizon, not asserted a.s. or in L¹. M is the specified finite sum, not an independent existential process.

constant_dependencies.original: The existential family θ may depend on all supplied data including K,fallback,f,T; no rate or universal numerical constant is claimed.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Constant dependencies: theta may depend on all data, including f,K,fallback,T; no uniform error rate or numerical constant.
